_translation_notes.bn_bengali: Standard Bengali (Bangla). Both 'bn' and 'bengali' keys are identical.
_translation_notes.brx_bodo: Bodo language in Devanagari script. Items marked _NOTE_brx need verification by a native Bodo speaker before shipping.

items._NOTE_bn: REVIEW NEEDED: 'জাপি' is an Assamese cultural item. Bengali patients may be unfamiliar. Consider adding a short description or image label for clarity.
items._NOTE_brx: REVIEW NEEDED: 'जापि' is a phonetic borrowing. Bodo communities may use their own term for a woven conical hat — verify with a native speaker.

items._NOTE_bn: REVIEW NEEDED: 'গামোছা' (gamosa) is the standard Bengali transliteration. The item is primarily an Assamese cultural symbol — Bengali patients may not recognise the term. Consider 'ঐতিহ্যবাহী গামোছা' for clarity.
items._NOTE_brx: REVIEW NEEDED: 'गामोसा' is the phonetic Bodo rendering. Bodo communities have the 'dokhona' as their own traditional cloth — verify if 'gamusa' is recognisable in Bodo cultural context.
REVIEW NEEDED: 'गेँदा' is the standard Hindi/Devanagari word for rhino. Verify the Bodo-specific term — some sources suggest 'गँड' (from Assamese 'গঁড়') is used in Bodo as well.

items._NOTE_bn: REVIEW NEEDED: 'ঢোল' is used in Bengali as well, but specifically the Bihu dhol is an Assamese instrument. Rendering as 'বিহু ঢোল' makes the cultural specificity explicit — verify if this is preferable to simply 'ঢোল'.
items._NOTE_brx: REVIEW NEEDED: Bodo communities also use the dhol ('खाम' is the Bodo traditional drum, distinct from the Bihu dhol). Using 'ढोल' as the recognisable loanword for the Bihu dhol specifically — verify if 'ढोल' or 'खाम' is more appropriate in context.
